title: near-miss field name (typo)
notes: One character from 'description' and the message is identical to E-SCHEMA-001. No 'did you mean'. Highest-value Fix win in the taxonomy. Location 1 -> 2 (phase-3 item 7): `  in descrption` is rendered and `prog.pdl:1` is that key's own mark. The path adds least here of anywhere in the corpus -- the key is at the top level, so it is a single segment that repeats the name already in the message. It is rendered anyway, because a renderer that suppressed one-segment paths would make the presence of the line carry meaning of its own. **Fix 0 -> 3.** The `help:` line is `did you mean `description:` instead of `descrption:`?`, which is the example `RUBRIC.md` prints under Fix 3 verbatim -- a specific, actionable edit rather than a pointer or a list. The candidates are the properties of the block the key is written on and nothing else: `descrption` is checked against `TextBlock`, which the discriminator selected from `text:`, so the answer is drawn from the same branch the complaint is. `difflib` at `_NEAR_MISS_CUTOFF`, the 0.7 already shared by `_near_miss`, `_import_missing` and E-SCHEMA-007, and `n=1`. Measured over the real pools rather than chosen by taste: a bench of 31 keys against the blocks they were written on answers 8 corrections at 0.7 and every one of them is right. Dropping to 0.6 adds no ninth correction and three wrong ones -- `parameters:` -> `parser:`, `params:` -> `parser:` and `id:` -> `kind:`, three different concepts read as three spellings. Raising to 0.8 keeps all 8 honest but loses two of them, `lans:` -> `lang:` and `num_iterations:` -> `maxIterations:`, and `tests/test_line_table.py` pins both as programs someone actually wrote. `n=1` for the same reason: at 0.6 the second-best match for `modle:` is `role:`, so a list of candidates is a list whose tail is noise. The three cases where it must stay silent are pinned by the sibling entry `E-SCHEMA-002-no-suggestion`. Location, what and why do not move: the message still does not say what fields a `text:` block *does* take, which is the Why 1.
